thread:
Ravi: FYI onboarding SolsticeX-Lite (3B) -> int4 hit a weird longcontext failure. Short generations look fine but beyond ~2048 tokens it starts repeating and ppl skyrockets. Anyone seen this pattern recently? :confused:
Nina: Could be rotary freq/base mismatch or tokenizer normalization. Do you have the convert command and model config?
Ravi: Convert we used: 
```
python tools/convert.py --src solsticex-lite/ --dst converted/solsticexx-int4/ --quant q4_0 --backend gptq
```
Model config has: 
```
{"rotary": {"base": 4096, "scale": 1.25}, "vocab_size": 51000}
```
Converter log: 
```
[WARN] rotary_base not present, defaulting to 10000
[INFO] using q4_0 symmetric scales
```
Hana: Defaulting to 10000 when model uses 4096 will cause aliasing much later, but weird that behavior collapses earlier. Any tokenizer anomalies?
Ravi: We discovered a small batch where ZWJ emoji sequences inserted extra token ids that map to idx 1 (reserved). Example: 
```
>>> tokenizer.encode("\ud83d\udc69\u200d\ud83d\udcbb hi")
[1023, 1, 1, 78]
```
The double 1s look like splitter artifacts.
Ollie: If tokenizer split into separate components, the token index stream sent to model won't match embedding table expected ordering if the converter or vocab roundtrip changed ordering. Also KV positions shift.
Kavita: We should check whether normalization (NFC vs NFKC) differs between training and conversion. Also check whether converter rewrites vocab.json ordering.
Nina: Quick tests: 1) force rotary.base=4096 in converted config and re-run longgen; 2) run sanitizer normalize('NFKC') before tokenization; 3) re-convert with per-channel scales (gptq preserving per-head).
Ravi: Ran (1) and (2) locally. With rotary base fixed, repeating reduced but ppl still high. After NFKC pre-normalize, the emo-split artifacts went away and ppl dropped another ~0.8.
Hana: Ran `tools/rotary_probe.py` against converted model to check headwise phase wrap: 
```
python tools/rotary_probe.py --model converted/solsticexx-int4/ --maxlen 8192 --emit-json
```
Output: 
```
{"head": 5, "wrap_pos": 2304, "delta_rad": 0.28}
```
That implies rotary base mismatch or per-head freq scaling gone.
Ollie: Try re-convert with `--preserve-rotary --preserve-perhead-scales` and asymmetric quant mode. Our int4 kernels have different dequant paths for asymmetric which preserve mean.
Ravi: Command used: 
```
python tools/convert.py --src solsticex-lite/ --dst converted/solsticexx-int4-asym/ --quant q4_0 --quant-mode asymmetric --preserve-rotary --preserve-perhead-scales
```
After that, headwise wrap vanished and longctx gen was stable to 6k in my quick smoke. PPLs: fp16 11.2, int4-asym 12.9.
Kavita: Good. Action items: 1) Patch converter to accept aliases: rotary.base, rotary_base, rotary_emb.base. 2) Add explicit check that vocab.json roundtrips and tokenization normalization (NFKC) is preserved. 3) Add `rotary_probe.py` to onboarding CI and fail if any head wrap_pos < model_context_len with delta_rad > 0.05.
Nina: I'll open PR for converter alias parsing and unit tests. Also adding a tiny test case with emoji+ZWJ pipeline to ensure no sentinel-like tokens appear after normalization.
Hana: Infra Bot, can you upload the conversion artifacts please?
Infra Bot: artifacts written to s3://redwood-artifacts/eng-ml/7177777777/solsticex-convert.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
Ollie: Note: we still see minor downstream rouge drop (~1 pt) on a handful of news summarization datasets. Might be expected quant noise but flagging for regression run before promoting.
Ravi: Filed follow-up tickets: RED-3301 (converter rotary aliases), RED-3302 (tokenizer nfkc default), RED-3303 (gptq perhead-asym flag). I'll add notes to the onboarding doc. Thanks all. :rocket:
